SBP: Confirms that son/daughter is health care proxy for father and the correct person to be speaking with.
When asked, makes a recommendation that focus of care be comfort and a Do Not Resuscitate order be enacted.
ICS: Elicits son’s/daughter’s understanding of father’s current medical condition with open-ended question(s).
Elicits son’s/daughter’s understanding of father’s values and preferences with open-ended question(s).
Describes father’s current medical condition with jargon-free language.
Informs son/daughter about prognosis of imminent death with direct, jargon free language.
Discusses resuscitation preferences/DNR orders with non-mechanistic simple language
Does NOT say, “Do you want us to do everything?”
Responds to son/daughter’s emotion with verbal empathic statement(s).
Responds to son/daughter’s emotion with non-verbal empathic behaviors (e.g. offering tissues, leaning in, light touch, respectful silence).
Informs son/daughter that goals of care will include all efforts to assure as much comfort as possible for father.
